applyTo: "server/public/**"
description: "Use when working on the HazMatIQ interface, layout, styling, interaction, or usability design. Favor polished, touch-friendly, low-overhead UI work that feels premium without expensive visual or runtime overhead."

# HazMatIQ UI guidance

- Keep the interface polished, readable, and operationally clear for time-critical field use.
- Favor plain HTML, CSS, and clean JavaScript patterns already used by the app; do not introduce framework churn for small UI edits.
- Prioritize clear hierarchy, strong contrast, large touch targets, and quick scanning of emergency data.
- Use efficient visual design: restrained animations, compact assets, and high-end style through layout and typography rather than heavy graphics.
- Avoid overloading the page with heavy motion, 3D effects, high-resolution assets, or complex JS libraries that slow down the app.
- Optimize for low resource usage and offline reliability while still delivering a premium, modern visual feel.
- Keep actions and status feedback obvious, especially for critical hazard information and plume or facility data.
- If a screen becomes cluttered, simplify the layout before adding more visual effects or controls.

When in doubt, choose the cleanest, fastest, most legible UI that still feels polished and trustworthy in a hazardous-response context.
